profile.summary: The RNAGym fitness leaderboard ranks sequence models by how well their scores agree with measured deep mutational scanning fitness on non-coding RNA assays. In version 0.1.1 the metric is the signed Spearman correlation between a model's score and the measured DMS fitness, averaged within each of three ncRNA categories (ribozyme, tRNA, aptamer) and then averaged over the three categories with equal weight. It is for someone choosing an RNA or genomic language model to score ncRNA variants without task-specific training.

summary_quotes.text: **Metric (updated in v0.1.1):** signed Spearman correlation between each model's score and the measured DMS fitness, macro-averaged over the 3 ncRNA categories (ribozyme, tRNA, aptamer), with each category weighted equally.
is an extensive benchmark suite and resource for RNA fitness and structure prediction

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a model's scores rank RNA variants in the same order as a wet-lab fitness measurement. The leaderboard keeps only assays whose readout reports the function of the RNA molecule itself: ribozyme cleavage, tRNA function and aptamer binding. Version 0.1.1 dropped the 37 mRNA-coding assays, because their readout is protein function, and the two mRNA-splicing assays, because their readout is a regulatory phenotype in human cells. Scores on the excluded assays are kept separately for reference.
sections.source_locator: leaderboard/fitness/README.md: Why we now exclude the mRNA assays

quotes.text: We restrict evaluation to assays whose DMS readout is a direct measure of the RNA molecule's own function (ribozyme cleavage, tRNA function, aptamer binding).
mRNA-coding (37 assays): the readout is protein function rather than mRNA fitness.

mRNA-splicing (2 assays, `Julien_2016_mRNA` and `Ke_2017_mRNA`): the readout is exon or alternative splicing efficiency in human cells, a regulatory phenotype rather than the molecular fitness of the mRNA itself.
Signed Spearman on the excluded assays is kept for reference

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The assays come from published deep mutational scanning experiments, one row each in the repository's reference sheet with an RNA type, the wild-type construct sequence, a description of the assay and, where one exists, a PDB structure and an Rfam family. The v0.1.1 leaderboard uses the three ncRNA categories: 26 ribozyme assays, 3 tRNA assays and 2 aptamer assays. Processed assay data, raw assay data, alignments, 3D structures, cross-validation splits for supervised use and the baselines' own predictions are distributed as separate downloads, and the data are also published as a Hugging Face dataset under CC BY 4.0.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: A model supplies one score per variant. Within an assay the score is correlated with the measured DMS fitness by Spearman correlation, keeping the sign, so a negative entry means the model ranks fit variants as unfit. Assay values are averaged within each category, and the headline number is the unweighted average of the three category means. All masked language models on the v0.1.1 board are scored the same way: the masked-marginal log-likelihood ratio, masking each mutated position one at a time in the variant's own sequence and summing over the variant's mutated positions. The leaderboard page says this convention matters because 99.4% of the ncRNA variants carry more than one mutation, and that RiNALMo and RNA-FM were rescored to reach it.

quotes.text: Signed, not absolute: a negative value means the model's score is negatively correlated with fitness.
Per category columns are the mean signed Spearman over the assays in that category; Macro is the unweighted average of the three category means.

All masked language models are now scored the same way: the masked-marginal log-likelihood ratio, with each mutated position masked one at a time in the variant's own sequence, summed over the variant's mutated positions.
This matters because 99.4% of the ncRNA variants are multi-mutants, which is exactly where scoring conventions differ.
RiNALMo and RNA-FM were rescored to reach that convention, and their earlier scoring scripts were replaced.

sections.title: Reported results
sections.body: Twelve models are listed. Evo 2 (40B) is first with a macro value of 0.2120, then RNA-ERNIE at 0.1937 and Evo 2 (7B) at 0.1904; GenSLM is last at -0.0338. The tRNA column holds the largest values for most models, for example 0.4310 for Evo 2 (40B) against 0.1081 on ribozymes. The page also reports all five released AIDO.RNA checkpoints on the same 31 assays, where the macro value rises with size at every step, from 0.0801 at 1M parameters to 0.1824 at 1.6B.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: Create the conda environment from the repository's rnagym_env.yml, download the processed assay data and the baselines' predictions from the project's download host, and aggregate with the script in fitness/. Note that the script at the pinned commit is the earlier one: it computes the absolute Spearman correlation for eight named models and writes results by RNA type, by mutation depth and by both. The leaderboard page says the v0.1.1 scoring scripts, and the performance_fitness.py that reproduces the signed ncRNA aggregate, are on the v0.2 branch.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: The files read describe none. The leaderboard is a zero-shot correlation against published DMS assays, and neither the leaderboard page nor the README says anything about whether a model's pretraining corpus contains the assayed sequences.

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: The leaderboard reports no intervals or replicates, only single values, and warns that differences below about 0.01 should not be read as separations. It also notes that the equal weighting gives the small tRNA and aptamer sets outsized, higher-variance weight. The aggregation script at the pinned commit has an optional flag to compute standard errors, which it describes as computationally intensive.

run_guide.summary: Get the repository at the pinned commit, build its conda environment, download the processed assay data and the baseline predictions, and run the repository's fitness aggregation script.
prerequisites: conda, to create the environment from the repository's rnagym_env.yml.
Python 3.8 or later, as the repository's badge states.
About 73MB for the processed assay data and 438MB for the model predictions, unzipped, as the README's table gives them.
The code is MIT licensed; the data on Hugging Face are CC BY 4.0.

steps.title: Aggregate per-assay performance
steps.shell:
python fitness/performance_fitness.py \
  --reference_file fitness/reference_sheet_final.csv \
  --combined_dir <folder holding one <DMS_ID>.csv per assay> \
  --performance_dir performance
steps.explanation: The flags are the four the script's argument parser defines. The script reads the reference sheet, then for each DMS_ID looks for <combined_dir>/<DMS_ID>.csv and correlates the DMS_score column with each model's score column. At this commit it reports the absolute Spearman correlation, AUC and MCC for eight named models and writes results by RNA type, by mutation depth and by both. It does not produce the signed ncRNA macro mean the v0.1.1 leaderboard publishes; the leaderboard page points to the v0.2 branch for that.

notes: Written from the RNAGym repository at commit 2828cf99316d75daaa8d832a2573cbb25bbd35fe, which is the commit the store's existing source already pins, and from the Hugging Face dataset record. The RNAGym paper is linked from the README only as bioRxiv 2025.06.16.660049 (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.06.16.660049v1); this run was told not to request bioRxiv, and a PMC search for the DOI 10.1101/2025.06.16.660049 returned no record, so no paper text was read. Two points for a human: the leaderboard page says its scoring scripts and the command that reproduces the aggregate are on a v0.2 branch, so the code at the pinned commit does not compute the published metric, and the record's own protocol names match the four structured entries here one to one. The per-category and macro values in the page's table match leaderboard_signed_3ncRNA.csv to four decimal places. The repository holds secondary and tertiary structure benchmarks as well; this record covers the fitness leaderboard only.
